findings.statement: Within the frozen RS-077 grid, every common-exact D/A pairing is exact under all five C coupling modes. C plus/minus direction is therefore not load-bearing for the bounded common scalar carrier.

No single one of D or A must always retain directional sign information. Common-exact candidates exist with D direction discarded and A direction retained, and with A direction discarded and D direction retained.

Every common-exact RS-077 candidate retains an orientation-sensitive coupling, SIGNED_NET or SEPARATED, in at least one of D or A. No common-exact candidate discards sign direction in both families simultaneously.
After the frozen partial order, the D/A Pareto frontier has four incomparable minima: TOTAL+SIGNED_NET, SIGNED_NET+TOTAL, ABS_NET+SEPARATED, and SEPARATED+ABS_NET.
The twelve full Pareto minima factor as three incomparable minimal C modes {TOTAL,SIGNED_NET,ABS_NET} times the four D/A Pareto minima; no unique common winner is selected.

6x3-k3 accepts all 125 coupling candidates and 4x5-k4 accepts 80, while horizontal-only 6x3-k4 accepts exactly the 65 common-exact candidates. Thus 6x3-k4 determines the present cross-carrier sign-coupling set.
Pareto-minimal sign coupling can reduce the 4x5-k4 structural image from rank 252 to 250 and the 6x3-k4 image from 14 to 13 while preserving scalar image dimensions 2 and 2.
TOTAL, SIGNED_NET, and ABS_NET must operate on the intervals represented by saturated symbols. Treating 1+, 2+, or 3+ as exact integers is not a valid quotient of the frozen RS-076 carrier.

nextQuestion: Can a small outcome-independent joint D/A circuit or canonical finite-pair relation factor all four D/A Pareto minima while preserving the scalar image, with C treated only through a structurally frozen member of its Pareto class?
